title: How the Titanic Worked: Part Two
summary: Part two of the Titanic series. The hosts pick up from the ship leaving Southampton and cover the April 14, 1912 voyage: the ice warnings received by Marconi wireless (and the overworked operators, Marconigrams, Cape Race), the calm, moonless night and lack of binoculars, the Moon and spring tide theory behind the 1912 iceberg glut, Fleet's sighting and Murdoch's maneuver, the side-swipe and the hull damage across five compartments, and Andrews' two-hour estimate. They then discuss evacuation and lifeboat loading under Smith and officers Murdoch and Lightoller, the passengers' disbelief, the Mount Temple and Californian controversy, Molly Brown and Robert Hitchens, Charles Joughin, the sinking itself, the Carpathia rescue, the body recovery, the US Senate and British inquiries, the vilification of J. Bruce Ismay, reforms like ice patrols and wireless operators, and Robert Ballard's discovery and proposal to preserve the wreck. The episode closes with the Morgan Robertson novella Futility and a call for reviews.

segments.title: Opening and recap of the Titanic's departure
segments.summary: The hosts open the episode, recap the ship's departure and early problems, and discuss Captain Edward Smith's reputation and the myth that he was speeding for a record.

segments.title: Ice warnings and Marconi wireless traffic
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Marconi wireless system, the ice warnings received on April 14, the Californian's message that it was surrounded by ice, and the heavy load of passenger Marconigrams sent through Cape Race.

segments.title: Calm, moonless night and the 1912 iceberg surge
segments.summary: The night was calm, clear and moonless with no binoculars in the crow's nest. The hosts discuss the Moon's close approach and spring tide that may have sent extra icebergs south that year.

segments.title: Collision and the side-swipe maneuver
segments.summary: Fleet spots the iceberg and Murdoch orders the engines stopped and reversed, turning the ship so it side-swipes the berg. The hosts discuss why that was done and how the damage occurred.

segments.title: Hull damage, flooding and the sinking timeline
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the estimated size of the hull breach, the five flooded compartments, the rivets, the buckling of the hull, and Thomas Andrews' estimate that the ship would sink in about two hours.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: A short break before the next section.

segments.title: Passenger disbelief and nearby ships
segments.summary: Most passengers and crew did not believe the ship was in danger. The hosts discuss the Carpathia's response, the Californian and the Mount Temple, and the blame placed on Stanley Lord.

segments.title: Lifeboat loading and chaos
segments.summary: The hosts describe the lifeboat counts and capacities, the early half-empty boats, the officers' different approaches to loading, the pistols carried by officers, and John Hart directing third-class passengers.

segments.title: Breaking apart, the sinking and the water
segments.summary: The hosts describe the stern rising, the bow filling and breaking off, the rapid descent to the seabed, the cries in the water, and the survivors' accounts. They discuss Molly Brown, Robert Hitchens refusing to go back, and Charles Joughin.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: A short break before the next section.

segments.title: Carpathia rescue, body recovery and inquiries
segments.summary: The Carpathia arrives and recovers survivors. The hosts discuss the recovery of bodies, the US Senate and British inquiries and their conclusion about lifeboats, and the vilification of J. Bruce Ismay.

segments.title: Reforms, wreck discovery and Robert Ballard
segments.summary: The hosts cover the reforms such as ice patrols and round-the-clock wireless operators, the discovery of the wreck by Robert Ballard, the iron-eating bacteria, and Ballard's proposal to paint the wreck to preserve it.

segments.title: Futility and the call for reviews
segments.summary: The hosts mention Morgan Robertson's novella Futility and its similarities to the Titanic, then ask listeners for reviews and ratings and to tell friends about the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and give the contact email.
